No single answer is universally accepted across sources. Authoritative organizations (e.g., The Vegan Society and peer‑reviewed reviews) state that vegans should obtain vitamin B12 via fortified foods or supplements because plant foods do not reliably provide it, implying supplementation is necessary for all vegans [d3,d4,d6,d8,d9]. In contrast, some popular sources argue that a well‑planned vegan diet can meet all nutrient needs without supplements, framing supplementation as optional depending on diet quality [d2,d5]. Additional guidance notes that certain minerals like calcium may warrant supplementation if dietary intake is insufficient, but this is not framed as universally required [d1].
